summary: Steel Aermotor tower built 1921; a 1955 newspaper names its North Mountain post and operator; register says later moved and rebuilt privately.

facts.status_note: Register says it was later moved and rebuilt privately; the Eastern US Lookouts list says removed, with no date.

events.note: Steel Aermotor tower built, per the FFLOS register.
Newspaper item dated April 13, 1955 names operator Nicholas Kravitz; the tower then covered North Mountain and southwest Wyoming County.
Registered on the FFLOS register September 16, 2008.

evidence.supports: built 1921 as a steel Aermotor tower, later moved and rebuilt privately
evidence.quote: This steel Aermotor tower was built in 1921 and later moved and rebuilt privately.

evidence.supports: register lists the location as Wyoming County, Pennsylvania
1955 item places the tower on North Mountain, names operator Nicholas Kravitz, and says it covered North Mountain and southwest Wyoming County
evidence.quote: Ricketts Tower, located on North Mountain, operator, Nicholas Kravitz. This tower covers North Mountain and Southwest Wyoming County.

evidence.supports: history lists the tower as removed, with no date
index lists Ricketts under Luzerne County
register is published by the Forest Fire Lookout Association

corrections.why: The register says the tower was later moved and rebuilt privately. That is not the same as gone, and no source says it was destroyed.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and the Ricketts history page say Wyoming County; the Pennsylvania R-Z index lists Ricketts under Luzerne County. The story follows the register and notes the index.
The register says the tower was moved and rebuilt privately; the Ricketts history page lists it as removed, with no date. The story gives both.

notes_for_editor: Brief coordinates (41.3765, -76.249) do not appear in either source; FFLOS says no coordinates are available, so they are unverified. The brief's gone status is proposed as relocated because the register describes a move and rebuild. No source describes the site or any surviving structure today. The operator name comes from a single 1955 newspaper quote.
